sections.workload:
每一次作业都需要花完整的一天（上午+下午+晚上）才能完成，类似于一个PA。大概是看需求、coding、训练、排错、再训练的过程。
不过如果用AI coding，或许只需要半天——还是建议自己动手写，因为final会考一道coding题，如果平时没有自己动手coding则很难做对

project可以2-3人group也可以一个人，vibe coding完成一个agent非常轻松，花1-2天即可完成整个project，主要需要思考复杂度和实用度。

每个月一个作业、最后一个月有一个作业和project，平时workload适中。

final只有两个小时，题量大。选择题有大量模棱两可的易错题，大题涉及数学/coding有点难。

sections.content:
In this current state, the teaching schedule is still way too messy and need a lot of readjusting on the timings. Of course you will very likely experience that by taking COMP 4901 courses, as you are basically a white rat anyway.

Class schedule:
Lecture 0: Introduction to Large Language Models
Lecture 1: Machine Learning Basics
Lecture 2: Language Model
Lecture 3: Neural Networks and Transformers
Lecture 4: Transformers
Lecture 5: Pretraining: Objectives and Data Curation
Lecture 6: Adapting Large Language Models
Lecture 7: Evaluation of Large Language Models
Lecture 8-9: Instruction Tuning and Alignment
Lecture 10: Reinforcement Learning Basics
Lecture 11: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
Lecture 12: Scaling up LLMs: Scaling Laws
Lecture 13: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
Lecture 14: Deep Reasoning Models
Lecture 15: Synthetic Data Training: Data Synthesis and Distillation
Lecture 16-17: LLM Agents
Lecture 18: LLM Bias and Safety
Lecture 19: LLM Safety, Attack, and Defence
Lecture 20: Hallucination and RAG
Lecture 21: RAG and MoE LLMs
Lecture 22: MoE LLMs, Vibe Coding, and Review

A lot of times, some topics are too long to be explained and thus just direct concatenated to the next topic, which I find very confusing when trying to do revision. I personally prefer the COMP 4901Y (now COMP 4551) syllabus which has a similar schedule (with addition of LLM optimization related stuff). However, I do like the coding examples and the project in this course.

A lot of time I just completely not understand what the math formulas even mean..... should have taken further MATH course instead of stuck with DSCT. I'm sure COMP3211 only helps in understanding reinforcement learning
sections.teaching:
The professor does write a lot of stuff on the lecture notes, and explain many of stuff in details(? or just repeating for better follow I guess). It is merely not my style of learning the materials, but I believe some people would like this teaching, so I won't downgrade it.

I won't say much about TA but they usually respond way faster than prof in email. They are also responsive in appealing my assignments.
sections.grading:
Grading is great if you are aiming for B range, and not if you are aiming for A range. I ended up getting a terrible grade due to how much I couldn't handle the teaching style.

Grading Scheme:
10% Attendance
40% Assignments
25% Mini Project
25% Final Exam

Attendance: 10/10
HW 1: 99/100
HW 2: 99/100
HW 3: 99/100
HW 4: 100/100
Group Project: 95/100
Final Exam: 57/100
(Mean: 61.40, Median: 64.50, SD: 15.2)

Almost everyone can get close to full mark in attendance, assignments and group project, so final exam becomes the only differentiator.

I admit this is my fault for not truly understand the course materials. I am just in full confusion due to the messy schedule. This is already my second time getting B range from Prof. He (I have only gotten 3 B range from COMP courses, rest are all A range)
sections.workload:
Attendance is required, but they do it by randomly give you iPRS quiz (not guarantee to have every lecture). You can try gamble that he won't give quiz if you want to skip one lecture.

Although homework takes the most time, the times taken are usually on the repeating training/fine-tuning for finding the best result. You can just let the training run and you can do anything else. I personally bought a laptop with good GPU to train it instead of using the clusters the department gives us.

Group project, while it sounds scary at the beginning, is actually quite simple. It is just an assignment without any given code and detailed instructions. You can do it individually, but you will not be awarded bonus points. You can also do it in groups of 2-3 people, but the grading between groupmates seems to depend on the work contributions. We are given an Deepseek api token, and all we do is to develop a conversation loops and tools to make an LLM agent. It is nothing special, but you can use this project to yap in interviews in the future.

Final exam is very hard to prepare for me, as there are no past papers and the slides are messy.
